headline: Profit rebounds as fee income offsets higher credit costs
summary_short: Western Alliance's Q2 FY2026 diluted EPS was $2.36 (+43% q/q, +14% y/y) on net income of $261.7M, as net interest income rose 14% y/y to $796.9M and the efficiency ratio improved to 58.0% from 60.1%. Provision for credit losses rose to $80.4M from $39.9M a year ago on higher charge-offs.
summary_long: Net interest income rose 14% y/y to $796.9M on $11.1B average earning-asset growth; NIM held flat at 3.53% as lower funding costs offset declining yields. Non-interest income grew $50.5M y/y to $198.8M on higher service fees and mortgage-banking gains. Non-interest expense rose $68.6M to $583.3M on higher deposit costs and salaries, but PPNR still climbed 24.5% y/y to $412.4M, pulling the efficiency ratio down to 58.0% from 60.1%. Provision for credit losses jumped to $80.4M from $39.9M a year ago on loan growth and charge-offs; H1's $293.6M figure includes two now-resolved one-off charge-offs (Leucadia $126.4M, Cantor Group $26.1M). CET1 held at 11.0%; dividend rose to $0.42/share. No new guidance was issued.
